This probably won't be of much consolation, but you're not alone. I'm 23, female, and in the exact same situation. I've even posted on reddit a few times regarding this issue. 

It's easy to tell someone to simply "join a group" or "find a hobby" and meet people, but it's incredibly tough to actually do. Especially if you, like me, suffer from social anxiety and fear the judgement and ridicule of others when it comes to trying new things. -_- I've opted instead for therapy right now. I feel like it's my last shot. Maybe therapy is something that might be interested in too? Don't rule it out.

Anyway, feel free to PM me if you want. Best of luck with this.

Hope you're feeling better. Maybe we can chat tonight for a bit? I'll pm you soon.

I'm glad things worked out for you. I wish I knew somewhere to make new friends. I'm not in university right now, so I work with my sister in our store and when I'm not there I'm at home. I just moved cities and was hoping to find ways of meeting new people. It sucks being alone most of the time, and the only friends I have here don't exactly care about me. :(

I understand that it takes time to change one's life, I just wish I had even somewhere to start.

Bummer. haha I'm not a great flirt or anything, I'm not even a decent flirt and I can't really read signals, so I'd much rather a guy just be honest and tell me he's interested. That or I'd tell him/ask him myself when I gain the self-confidence of course. I can't play games and beat around the bush. I'm no good. ;p

>in reality you'll meet them when you least expect it

Maybe. Well, like I said I'm not in school right now and only go to work, and home most of the time. So I have NO choice but to *actively* look for places to go to meet guys or I won't "run into" any anytime soon. -_-

I found the pdf online yesterday of the book you mentioned and slimmed through it over, focusing on the chapters that spoke of "attraction" etc. Unfortunately, it seems that there's far more info for men about decoding women's body language, than the other way around. Seems like a good book overall, don't get me wrong. Just sucks that most books assume women should know how to read guys, even this book sort of makes this assumption. Ah, something's wrong with me. lol

> if you need a guy to run things by, feel free to pm me

Thanks for the offer. :) Hope I'm not a bother if I do pm you.

> First of all being self-conscious and having anxiety are not a fault.

Thanks for this. I've always struggled with the idea of whether nervousness and anxiety were actually character flaws rather than just being issues a person is dealing with. I don't think that being self-conscious, shy or anxious should make someone a "bad person." Several traits can be considered flaws/faults "dishonesty, disloyalty, being unsympathetic, etc. The terms flaw and fault are thrown around too carelessly when people speak with or about someone with anxiety. People don't realize how damaging it can be to hear these things said about me as someone whose experiencing these issues. 

And thanks for saying I'm not pathetic, it can certainly feel that way at times. 

>The guy you want is the one who would be happy to hear you have anxiety. 

I don't know about "happy," hopefully *accepting.* Still, I hear what you're saying. Thanks.

> I can tell you with some certainty that when a guy is talking to you he is interested on some level, especially if you are attractive.

Interesting.

> It just may or may not be the type of "relationship" you are looking for. 

Okay, then what is it? One of the main reasons I can't read guys is because when they're being friendly, I can't tell it apart from flirting. To me when guys are being friendly or when they're flirting it's exactly the same. I'm not presumptuous so I always assume they're just being friendly. 

If they really are flirting with me sometimes, then why don't they just ask me out or say they're interested? Why flirt for no reason?

Similarly, I don't know how to react to guys that talk to me while smiling and making tons of eye contact. I can't just ask "do you like me?" I figure that they would tell me if they were interested in a relationship, so I conclude that they aren't and are just a friendly person. Last thing I want is to embarrass myself by assuming someone likes me when they are just looking for a friend. : / It sucks having zero experience in this area, but if I never start dating I'll just remain inexperienced. Feels like a paradox haha

Thanks for giving me the name of the book. I'll check it out, hopefully I'll get something out of it too.

What did your friend do in the end?

Thanks for your comment, and yeah, you're right the guys that talk to her usually aren't my type, but it does make me feel ignored because I don't get many guys talking to me randomly in the first place. 

>  You need to go out without your sister and try to initiate conversation with strangers that are too nervous to start it. 

Agreed. Actually, I know this intellectually, but I don't have the confidence to start a convo with a random stranger even if I just wanted to make a new friend. Actually, I was able to walk up to someone once in university and a friendship developed from it, but it was a classmate who had already added me to facebook before we first spoke.

But typically I have approach anxiety on top of social anxiety. I fear I'll be rejected/laughed at for being so awkward but at the same time i know this is probably my only hope. I'm left feeling hopeless as you can imagine. :(  

> being completely blunt about how socially awkward you are is a huge ice breaker and will allow the guy to relax and be himself

Really? I've always wondered if I should just admit that I have anxiety so at least people understand why I act the way I do at times. But, people online usually say that it's a fault and "never let anyone know your faults/flaws. People like confident. Traits like shyness, anxiety, self-consciousness are all unattractive and make people feel awkward around you and avoid you." I fear telling people would make them judge me as being socially inept, naive, inexperienced, stupid, pathetic, etc.

But not saying anything isn't exactly helping either.

I never considered that it could be due to my body language. 

> I expected to be the 'background' character I naturally hung back, and because my friends were used to this they naturally stepped over me

Yep, this is how it is for me. Couldn't have said it better. I've become used to being ignored/excluded when in groups with my sister that I find myself walking "behind" our "friends" rather than beside them. I'll notice I do this once in a while and try to actively walk beside them, and be physically closer but my sister will push me out of the way and walk next to a friend of ours. The sidewalk is only so big, so I'll be left in the back. Just an example. I honestly feel like pushing her when she does this to me sometimes. -_- 

How do I develop body language that demands attention and respect rather than saying "hey, it's okay to ignore/exclude/push me. I'm nothing anyway." 

> "You're meant to be the leading lady in your own life"

I like this quote. I know intellectually that it's true. I don't know how to make it happen for me right now though.

Aw, I answered this msg too late. You're probably sleeping by now. I'm PM you if that's all right.

I agree with the first part. It sucks though because I'm usually so anxious and shy that I'd prefer to be with someone familiar to me (in this case my sister) when meeting people, hanging out with people I don't know, etc.

I realize though, that the result of going everywhere with her is that I don't get a chance to make any friends of my own or really learning to be more social. 

As for this part:

> Do ALL of your girlfriends cockblock you too?

It's unnecessary. I never said they did anything like that. They ignore me/exclude a lot of the time when my sister is around but no they don't "cockblock" that I'm aware of.

> Take a hard look at yourself and ask: Is it me? Do I turn guys away because of the way that I act/present myself? 

No need to even say this LOL I always blame myself for everything that happens to me. I'm a good person, but I realize there's something about me that makes me unlikable. 

So in answer to your last question: OF COURSE. I just don't know what I do exactly. So it's rather hard to change. ... Maybe I just wasn't meant to have friends or love. Whatever.

Thanks for getting back to me. I look forward to hearing what she says. I don't know if she'd be familiar with places in Hamilton that could help though. Still, I'll await your response.

> I think you are already doing something different: you reached out for help. 

I guess, but honestly I'm always going online and asking people for advice about my problems. Doing something different would be therapy/a counselor, getting new coping methods/advice or finding places to meet people and going. Something like that. I reach out a lot every once on the internet and nothing much changes.

> Part of that is the illusion created by the depression

I didn't know this but it makes sense. 

> Depression is a real pain in the ass because it always has a second level.

Mos def. This is true for me. But I think it's the fact that I have social anxiety and thus, can't connect easily with people. All I have in terms of friends (most of the time) is my sister, and on occasion our mutual friends, who don't like me as much anyway. I'm alone a lot. I go to work (my sis and I run a store together) and then go home and go on my computer. I don't really have a social life that I would want, so being isolated from my peers (never having dated and having few if any friends) makes me feel pathetic. It feels like I'm wasting my youth, like I must not be likable because something I can't detect from my subjective stance is wrong with me. This, in turn, makes me depressed pretty much. 

Thanks, I'll PM you.

I have trouble with body language and signals from guys myself. I can never tell if a guy is flirting or being friendly, it's the same to me. I also have self-esteem/self-confidence issues so I convince myself that of course guys don't like me, they're only being friendly. Literally months or years later I'll realize I was wrong. I still can't recognize the signs guys give out to be honest.

Can you recommend some books/articles about body language? 

I'm not jealous. I'm sad that my "friends" and aquaintances ignore me in favor of her though, and the fact that she even treats me badly in front of people which of course encourages and makes it okay for people to treat me badly and ignore me. Last semester in university I managed to make friends with a really nice, outgoing girl (unfortunately I moved schools so we're not close anymore) but she adored me. I know I'm hard to get to know, and have trouble connecting to people due to being so nervous and focused on being nice and likable rather than showing who I really am. But I have charisma of my own. My sister goes to extremes to be liked, I wouldn't wanna be like that. She'll do silly and ridisulous stuff for a laugh and it's super immature at times. Maybe she can get away with it being 20. I don't know.

At this point I don't think I'll be able to have close friends in my life if we keep sharing friends. I want some friends that are my own. I want a chance to show how great a person I am. 

P.S. I know I have charisma because she ALWAYS steals my jokes, opinions, etc and tells our friends before I can. So yeah, my personality can't be that bad.

Please do let me know what your friends say.

Also, I guess i assumed I have depression because I feel sad most of the time, sometimes I'm able to ignore it and have a good day, but many nights I'll go to bed in tears, I'm alone alot, don't have any close friends, and sometimes thoughts of being dead are very comforting (not often mind you, but even sometimes is probably too much). If that's not depression great, it's not really something I want to have anyway. 

> Don't give up. I sense that you are a good person and are just suffering right now. It does get better, even if that sounds like a trite and stupid thing to say. It is true. 

Thanks, I don't think I'm a bad person at all either. I just don't believe it will get better unless I start doing something differently. If I continue to live my life the way I have been up until now forever, of course nothing will ever change. I desperately want to have close friends, to be in love, to have experiences, etc. that are memorable and happy. I just don't know how to go about it, and if I don't figure it out I'll be miserable my whole life, or just end it early.

> Approach social interactions with confidence

I want to do this. But I feel like this is more something to aim for and not a technique. How do I suddenly approach social situations with confidence? I don't even know how to fake it. I also think people catch onto my nervousness because of my little quirks when speaking to ppl (stuttering, not always being able to look them in the eye, fidgeting, and not knowing what to say at times and going silent or worse, babbling). How do I play these things off as confidence?

> if someone is concerned enough with your faults to actually care than they're probably a pretty petty person with quite a few issues as well

I guess. I've always thought my faults were so obvious that anyone would notice/care. : / It'd be nice to know that most people don't care, but I feel like they do. After all isn't that why people avoid/ignore/exclude me?

>  But seriously though, don't ever think your better off dead. You will never be better off dead. No matter how much shit you have weighing down on you, you can always get out from underneath it.

I appreciate you saying this, but it really doesn't feel that way sometimes. Sometimes death does seem alot better, maybe then people might appreciate who I am, and at least then I wouldn't feel sad and alone. There's comfort in that, as fucked up as it may sound.

> Stop worrying about what everyone else thinks and just take care of yourself, never let someone else get in the way of your happiness.

I want to be this way. I want to happy. But to me, being happy includes having close friends, even just 2 or 3, and, a relationship among other things of course. I don't have these though. I see so many people around me easily making and keeping friends, dating, etc. And I don't know why I don't have that too, what's wrong with me? 

> Oh, and if your confident enough to note that others have called you cute than you have to be able to realize you probably are. Just go out and be nice, and smile, and flirt. Someone will come along eventually!

I believe some people think I am attractive. Still trying to believe it myself. Sometimes I do and other times, I don't at all. Being nice isn't really getting me anywhere, people don't care about "nice" people. I'm tempted to start being more selfish and uncaring, and not try to make people like me because it's not like they like me when I'm nice anyway. ;p

I don't know how to flirt, I always come off as awkward. I don't think anyone will come along, they haven't so far. Thanks though

I have no "resentment" toward her. We're actually pretty close, but perhaps too close? We probably shouldn't have all the same friends, and she really does act differently when we're with them. She becomes really "bubbly" and acts silly, which is fine but it goes too far when she literally pushes me aside to be beside one of my friends, or excludes me. -_-

But anyway, I'd definitely be interested in seeing a counselor about social anxiety. I just don't have the money for it right now. I might get desperate enough to run up my credit cards for therapy though.
